claim: For fixed \(p_0>0\) and \(q>0\), every integer \(n\ge\max\{2,p_0\}\), and model parameters \(b,c_0>0\), let \(B\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}\) have \(B_{ii}=1\) and independent \(B_{ij}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_0/n)\) for \(i\ne j\). Define \(S_{ij}=\sum_{k\ne i}B_{ki}B_{kj}\), \(K_R=\exp\!\big(p_0[\exp(2+p_0(e-1))-1]\big)\), \(K_C=\exp\!\big(p_0(e-1)+p_0[\exp(1+p_0(e-1))-1]\big)\), and \(u_n=(q+1)\log n+\log(K_R+K_C)\). In the homogeneous quadratic-benefit, quadratic-cost networked public-goods model of Cheng, Deng, and Ma, if \(c_0/(2b)>u_n\), then the Nash equilibrium is unique with probability at least \(1-n^{-q}\).

integrity.proof_basis: Analytic moment-generating-function bounds, a union bound, the induced matrix norm inequality, and the stated uniqueness criterion.
integrity.unproved_extensions: No claim is made for dependent edges, heterogeneous model parameters, or sharpness.

scientific_limitations: The explicit constants are conservative and are not optimized.
The bound is sufficient, not necessary or sharp.
The result assumes independent directed off-diagonal Bernoulli entries with fixed \(p_0\) and fixed \(q\).
title: A logarithmic uniqueness threshold for sparse random networked public-goods games
